plain_text: Phytochrome proteins flip shape between red and far-red light, letting photosynthetic cells tell open sun from a rival's shadow.
source: Rockwell, Su & Lagarias (2006) Annu. Rev. Plant Biol. 57:837; Butler et al. (1959) PNAS 45:1703
note: Bacterial phytochromes predate land plants; plants later use the same switch to trigger shade-avoidance growth and germination.

plain_title: A single cell steers toward the light
plain_text: A green alga catches photons with a light-gated ion channel and bends its twin flagella within milliseconds to swim into bright water.
source: Nagel et al. (2003) PNAS 100:13940; Sineshchekov, Jung & Spudich (2002) PNAS 99:8689
note: Measured in living Chlamydomonas; neuroscientists later borrowed channelrhodopsin for optogenetics.

plain_title: Slow action potentials in green algae
plain_text: Stonewort algae, close aquatic cousins of land plants, fire all-or-nothing electrical spikes down 10-centimetre cells that pause internal streaming.
signalling_channel: Ca2+-activated Cl- efflux & K+ repolarisation (~2 cm/s)
source: Beilby (2007) Plant Cell Environ. 30:435; Cole & Curtis (1938) J. Gen. Physiol. 22:37
note: Studied electrically since the 1930s, fourteen years before Hodgkin and Huxley's squid-axon model.

plain_title: Microscopic mouths weigh water against carbon
plain_text: Millions of paired guard cells on every leaf open and close pores by pumping potassium ions, trading carbon intake against drying out.
signalling_channel: ABA hormone + blue-light H+-ATPase + K+/anion turgor loop
source: Hetherington & Woodward (2003) Nature 424:901; Ruszala et al. (2011) Curr. Biol. 21:1030
note: Fossil stomata appear on Silurian–Devonian stems ~420–407 million years ago.

plain_title: Roots and fungi trade sugar for minerals
plain_text: Fungal threads extend plant roots a hundredfold to mine phosphorus in exchange for sugar; how much neighbouring trees warn each other through them remains debated.
signalling_channel: Strigolactone chemical handshake + peri-arbuscular phosphate/hexose exchange
source: Remy et al. (1994) PNAS 91:11841; Kiers et al. (2011) Science 333:880; Karst, Jones & Hoeksema (2023) Nat. Ecol. Evol. 7:501
note: 407-Myr Rhynie chert fossils preserve fungal arbuscules inside plant cells; Karst et al. (2023) caution that forest-wide 'mother tree' warning claims outrun field evidence.

milestone: Root-apex multi-gradient foraging & statolith gravity sensing
plain_title: Root tips steer toward water and nutrients
plain_text: Without a brain, each growing root tip weighs gravity with starch grains and bends toward water, nitrate and phosphate while avoiding salt and stones.
representative_system: Vascular plant root cap & transition zone
source: Darwin & Darwin (1880) The Power of Movement in Plants; Muthert et al. (2020) Front. Plant Sci. 10:1807
note: True roots evolve independently in lycophytes and euphyllophytes during the Early Devonian.

plain_title: A chewed leaf warns the rest of the plant
plain_text: When a caterpillar bites one leaf, spilled glutamate opens glutamate-receptor channels along the veins, sending a calcium wave to distant leaves within two minutes.
signalling_channel: Vascular glutamate -> GLR Ca2+ wave (~1 mm/s) -> jasmonate defense burst
source: Toyota et al. (2018) Science 361:1112; Mousavi et al. (2013) Nature 500:422
note: Uses plant relatives of the same glutamate receptors that carry fast excitatory signals in animal brains.

milestone: Seed dormancy coat & ABA/GA thermal-time integrator
plain_title: Seeds wait for the right season to sprout
plain_text: A seed weighs moisture, chill and daylight through two opposing hormones so it does not sprout into a fatal drought or late frost.
signalling_channel: Abscisic acid (hold) vs gibberellin (grow) bistable hormone switch
source: Finch-Savage & Leubner-Metzger (2006) New Phytol. 171:501; Linkies et al. (2010) New Phytol. 186:817
note: Some viable seeds (such as Judean date palms) have sprouted after ~2,000 years of dry dormancy.

plain_title: Plants count the weeks of winter in chromatin
plain_text: Many plants refuse to flower until they feel weeks of winter cold, progressively silencing a brake gene with histone marks that persist through cell divisions until spring.
signalling_channel: Cell-autonomous digital Polycomb histone methylation counter
source: Angel, Song, Dean & Howard (2011) Nature 476:7358; Bastow et al. (2004) Nature 427:164
note: Each cell switches its FLC locus off probabilistically in the cold, so the fraction of silenced cells records winter duration.

plain_text: Chewed leaves release airborne green-leaf scents that prime neighbouring branches on the same plant—and nearby eavesdropping plants—to ready bitter toxins early, and summon parasitic wasps.
source: Karban et al. (2000) Oecologia 125:66; Heil & Silva Bueno (2007) PNAS 104:5467; Turlings et al. (1990) Science 250:1251
note: Ecologically acts first as within-plant self-signalling across branches whose vascular links do not connect directly.

milestone: Multimodal floral colour, scent, nectar & electric-field cues
plain_title: Flowers advertise honestly to flying pollinators
plain_text: Flowers combine ultraviolet bullseyes, tailored scents, measured nectar rewards and weak electrostatic fields that tell a bee whether another bee just visited.
signalling_channel: UV/visible petals + volatile terpenes + floral electrostatic step (~30 mV)
source: Clarke, Whitney, Sutton & Robert (2013) Science 340:66; Bao et al. (2019) PNAS 116:24707
note: Bumblebees detect the weak electric-charge change left on a flower for ~100 seconds after a previous bee lands.

milestone: Venus flytrap two-touch action-potential calcium counter
plain_title: A carnivorous plant that counts to five
plain_text: A Venus flytrap ignores a single raindrop: two hair touches within 20 seconds snap the trap shut, and five touches switch on digestive enzymes.
signalling_channel: Mechanosensitive ion channels -> 0.1 m/s action potentials -> cytosolic Ca2+ threshold counter
source: Böhm et al. (2016) Curr. Biol. 26:286; Hedrich & Neher (2018) Trends Plant Sci. 23:220; Suda et al. (2020) Nat. Plants 6:1219
note: Droseraceae carnivorous traps diverged ~65–85 Ma; calcium decays with a ~20 s time constant, acting as a single-cell leaky integrator.

milestone: Dodder parasitic vine host-scent foraging & mRNA bridge
plain_title: A leafless vine smells its host and swaps thousands of RNAs
plain_text: Parasitic dodder seedlings sniff airborne host volatiles to grow toward tomato over wheat, then plug into the host's veins and exchange thousands of messenger RNAs.
signalling_channel: Chemotropic volatile steering + haustorial plasmodesmata mRNA/protein stream
source: Runyon, Mescher & De Moraes (2006) Science 313:1964; Kim et al. (2014) Science 345:808
note: Studied in living Cuscuta; shows systemic macromolecules crossing species boundaries through grafted phloem.

milestone: Mimosa pudica rapid turgor collapse & drop habituation
plain_title: A touch-shy plant stops flinching at harmless drops
plain_text: Sensitive-plant leaves fold in a tenth of a second when touched, yet if dropped harmlessly again and again they stop folding while still reacting to a pinch.
signalling_channel: Action potential + pulvinar aquaporin K+/Cl- water efflux (~2–10 cm/s)
source: Hagihara et al. (2022) Nat. Commun. 13:6412; Gagliano et al. (2014) Oecologia 175:63
note: Whether long-term drop habituation represents associative-like memory or receptor/energetic adaptation remains actively debated.
